type: re-test of C106 and C107 with the dead feature removed

withdrawn.C107: the fair-tree hardening, which rested on the same dead-feature design

kept.C105: the fully-informed redundancy is exact only for linear models; R137 gave +0.0152 and this run reproduces +0.0152 exactly, so it rests on a clean comparison
kept.C115: pathway over target under both families, measured with grouping-only features
kept.C113_C114: pathway over target in the ridge rounds
kept.frozen claim: unaffected, it is a ridge result and was always labelled as such

why_the_earlier_null_arose: R138 and R139 put drug identity codes into the no-identity arm, and on evaluation rows every one of those codes was the reserved -1, a dead feature
new_finding: the decay shape is the same in both families: near zero when fully informed (0.000 ridge, 0.015 tree) and near 0.1 when absent (0.13 ridge, 0.098 tree)

lesson.class: a dead feature in one arm can manufacture a model-family difference
lesson.escalation: the ninth rule was written down two rounds before it was actually executed, so it must become check code rather than prose

limits: Sixty splits, one untrained-free tree configuration, integer coding.
Conditions A and B use different evaluation pools, so this compares gains rather than arms in one pool.
Retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim.
next_gate: write a reusable check that reports each feature's dispersion on the evaluation set before any multi-arm comparison
